'''Jordan Grayson Mickey''' (born July 9, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Qingdao Eagles]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He played college basketball for the [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU Tigers]] before being selected by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 33rd overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]].

==High school career==
Mickey attended [[Grace Preparatory Academy|Arlington Grace Prep]] for three years, guiding the program to a state championship during his junior season, before transferring to [[Prime Prep Academy]] in 2012. During his lone campaign with Prime Prep in 2012–13, he averaged 16 points, 10 rebounds and two blocks per game.<ref name=draft-profile>{{cite web|title=Draft Profile: Jordan Mickey|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/draft/profile-jordan-mickey|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 30, 2016}}</ref> Considered a four-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Mickey was listed as the No. 12 power forward and the No. 38 player in the nation in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jordan Mickey Recruiting Profile|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/104932/jordan-mickey|work=ESPN.com|access-date=July 11, 2015}}</ref>

==College career==
Mickey was an immediate contributor when he began his freshman season at [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]] in 2013–14, compiling double-doubles during each of his first three contests. He started all 34 of the Tigers' games and averaged 12.7 points and 7.9 rebounds per game. He also became just the second Tiger in program history to block at least 100 shots in a season, joining [[Shaquille O'Neal]].<ref name="draft-profile" /> He earned multiple awards in 2013–14, including Coaches All-SEC Second Team, All-SEC Freshman Team, All-SEC Defensive Team, LSWA Louisiana Freshman of the Year, and LSWA All-Louisiana Second Team.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|title=#25 Jordan Mickey|url=http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208645261|work=lsusports.net|access-date=January 30, 2016|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304052743/http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208645261|url-status=dead}}</ref>

As a sophomore in 2014–15, Mickey led the nation in blocked shots per game (3.6), along with 15.4 points and 9.9 rebounds. He blocked at least six shots in four straight contests from December 18 through January 3. He did, however, suffer with lingering shoulder and ankle injuries throughout his sophomore year, but played through the pain.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rosetta|first1=Randy|title=Former LSU big man Jordan Mickey goes to the Celtics early in the 2nd round|url=http://www.nola.com/lsu/index.ssf/2015/06/former_lsu_forward_jordan_mick.html|access-date=June 27, 2015|work=NOLA.com|date=June 25, 2015}}</ref> In the second round of the NCAA Tournament, he tallied 12 points, 14 rebounds and six blocks, but the Tigers were edged by [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|North Carolina State]], 66–65.<ref name="draft-profile" /> He again earned multiple awards in 2014–15, including Coaches All-SEC First Team, AP All-SEC First Team, All-SEC Defensive Team, All-District NABC Team, and All-District USBWA Team.<ref name="bio" />

On March 31, 2015, Mickey declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Vecenie|first1=Sam|title=LSU's Jordan Mickey declares for NBA Draft|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25130419/lsus-jordan-mickey-declares-for-nba-draft|access-date=January 30, 2016|work=CBSSports.com|date=March 31, 2015}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Boston Celtics (2015–2017)===

====2015–16 season====
On June 25, 2015, Mickey was selected with the 33rd overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-select-rozier-hunter-mickey-and-thornton-2015-draft|title=Celtics Select Rozier, Hunter, Mickey and Thornton in 2015 Draft|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2015|access-date=June 26, 2015}}</ref> On July 20, he signed with the Celtics after playing for the team at the Utah and Las Vegas summer leagues.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-2015-draft-pick-jordan-mickey|title=Celtics Sign 2015 Draft Pick Jordan Mickey|work=NBA.com|date=July 20, 2015|access-date=July 20, 2015}}</ref> Over the first two and a half months of the 2015–16 season, Mickey spent the majority of his time in the [[NBA Development League]] playing for the [[Maine Red Claws]], Boston's affiliate team in the D-League.<ref name=assign>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 26, 2017|archive-date=March 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322122733/http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Between October 28 and January 18, he played three games for the Celtics and 21 games for the Red Claws.

On January 5, 2016, Mickey was named the NBA Development League Player of the Month for December 2015, becoming the first player in Red Claws franchise history to receive Player of the Month honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/jordan-mickey-named-nba-d-league-player-of-the-month/n-5086297|title=Jordan Mickey Named NBA D-League Player of the Month|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=January 5, 2016|access-date=January 30, 2016}}</ref> Mickey led Maine to a 7–2 record (6–2 in games that he played) and averaged 19.6 points, 10.5 rebounds, 5.3 blocks and 1.8 assists per game. On December 6, he scored a season-high 32 points and grabbed 13 rebounds in a 110–97 win over the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]], and on December 31, he recorded a triple-double with 13 points, 13 rebounds and an NBA D-League season-high 10 blocks in a 119–112 win over the [[Texas Legends]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/maines-jordan-mickey-named-nba-development-league-player-of-the-month/|title=Maine's Jordan Mickey Named NBA Development League Player of the Month|work=NBA.com|date=January 5, 2016|access-date=January 30, 2016}}</ref> On January 18, he was recalled by the Celtics after he sprained his ankle two days prior while playing for the Red Claws.<ref>{{cite news|last1=King|first1=Jay|title=Jordan Mickey recalled by Boston Celtics for treatment on ankle injury|url=http://www.masslive.com/celtics/index.ssf/2016/01/jordan_mickey_recalled_by_bost.html|access-date=January 30, 2016|work=MassLive.com|date=January 18, 2016}}</ref> On January 29, he was named in the East All-Star team for the 2016 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star Game]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2016-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|title=Sixteen NBA Veterans Headline Rosters for NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented By Kumho Tire|work=NBA.com|date=January 29, 2016|access-date=January 29, 2016|archive-date=February 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170207115139/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2016-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|url-status=dead}}</ref> becoming the 13th player in Red Claws' history to land an All-Star honor.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Forsberg|first1=Chris|title=Celtics coach Brad Stevens thinks highly of D-League All-Star Jordan Mickey|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4721860/celtics-coach-brad-stevens-thinks-highly-of-d-league-all-star-jordan-mickey|access-date=January 30, 2016|work=ESPN.com|date=January 29, 2016}}</ref> However, he was ruled out of the All-Star game due to his left ankle injury and was replaced in the East team by [[Keith Benson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/keith-benson-quinn-cook-nba-dleague-all-star-replacements/|title=Keith Benson and Quinn Cook Named as All-Star Replacements|work=NBA.com|date=February 5, 2016|access-date=February 5, 2016|archive-date=February 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160206044825/http://dleague.nba.com/news/keith-benson-quinn-cook-nba-dleague-all-star-replacements/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Mickey went on to play in seven of the Celtics' 10 games post All-Star break, receiving limited minutes. During this stretch, he recorded a season-best three blocked shots in under two minutes of action against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on March 9.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160309/MEMBOS/gameinfo.html|title=Celtics win 14th straight at home, beat Grizzlies 116-96|work=NBA.com|date=March 9, 2016|access-date=March 10, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310104151/http://www.nba.com/games/20160309/MEMBOS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 10, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> The following day, he returned to the Red Claws for the first time since January 18<ref>{{cite news|url=https://twitter.com/celtics/status/708028673069346817|title=The Boston Celtics have assigned Coty Clarke...|work=Twitter|date=March 10, 2016|access-date=March 11, 2016}}</ref> for a one-game stint.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://twitter.com/celtics/status/708351866359422976|title=The Boston Celtics have recalled forwards Coty...|work=Twitter|date=March 11, 2016|access-date=March 11, 2016}}</ref> He received three more assignments to Maine on March 13, April 5 and April 7.<ref name="assign" /> In 25 games (23 regular season, two playoff) for Maine in 2015–16, he averaged 17.8 points, 10.2 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 3.9 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/m/mickejo01d.html|title=Jordan Mickey D-League Stats|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=June 9, 2016}}</ref>

====2016–17 season====
Mickey appeared in eight of the Celtics' first 19 games of the 2016–17 season. During that stretch, he scored a season-high eight points on 4-of-4 shooting in 19 minutes against the [[Denver Nuggets]] on November 6.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mickejo01/gamelog/2017/|title=Jordan Mickey 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 3, 2016}}</ref> On January 11 against Washington, Mickey made his first career start as a replacement for the injured [[Amir Johnson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-jordan-mickey-will-start-at-power-forward-wednesday/|title=Celtics' Jordan Mickey: Will start at power forward Wednesday|work=CBSSports.com|date=January 11, 2017|access-date=January 11, 2017}}</ref> In 14 minutes, he recorded four points, two rebounds, one assist and one block in a 117–108 win over the Wizards.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400900004|title=Wizards vs. Celtics – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=January 11, 2017|access-date=January 11, 2017}}</ref> During the 2016–17 season, he received multiple assignments to the [[Maine Red Claws]], the Celtics' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 11, 2017|archive-date=January 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On July 13, 2017, Mickey was waived by the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-jordan-mickey-waived-by-celtics/|title=Celtics' Jordan Mickey: Waived by Celtics|work=CBSSports.com|date=July 13, 2017|access-date=July 13, 2017}}</ref>

===Miami Heat (2017–2018)===
On August 20, 2017, Mickey signed with the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-jordan-mickey-0|title=HEAT Signs Jordan Mickey|work=NBA.com|date=August 20, 2017|access-date=August 20, 2017}}</ref> On December 16, 2017, he scored a career-high nine points off the bench in a 90–85 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975183|title=Richardson scores 28 points, Heat beat Clippers 90-85|work=ESPN.com|date=December 16, 2017|access-date=December 17, 2017}}</ref> In May 2018, the Heat declined their $1.6 million option on Mickey's contract, making him a free agent.<ref>{{cite web|last=Winderman|first=Ira|url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-jordan-mickey-s20180510-story.html|title=Heat decline option on Jordan Mickey, making him a free agent|work=sun-sentinel.com|date=May 10, 2018|access-date=June 24, 2018}}</ref>

===Khimki (2018–2019)===
On July 26, 2018, Mickey signed a one-year deal with the Russian team [[BC Khimki]] of the [[VTB United League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Jordan Mickey joined BC Khimki|url=https://en.bckhimki.ru/news/clubnews/2018/july/1331/|website=bckhimki.ru|access-date=July 26, 2018|date=July 26, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8whjfht3rlcxygnu/khimki-tabs-athletic-big-man-mickey|title=Khimki tabs athletic big man Mickey|website=EuroLeague.net|access-date=July 26, 2018|date=July 26, 2018}}</ref>

===Real Madrid (2019–2020)===
On July 15, 2019, Mickey signed a two-year deal with Spanish powerhouse [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Official Announcement: Jordan Mickey {{!}} Real Madrid CF |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/07/official-announcement-jordan-mickey |access-date=15 July 2019 |work=Real Madrid C.F. - Web Oficial}}</ref>

===Return to Khimki (2020–2021)===
On July 21, 2020, Mickey made his official return to [[BC Khimki|Khimki Moscow]] on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jordan Mickey returns to Khimki Moscow |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jordan-mickey-returns-to-khimki-moscow/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 21, 2020 |date=July 21, 2020 |last1=Lupo |first1=Nicola }}</ref>

===Zenit St. Petersburg (2021–2022)===
On July 4, 2021, Mickey signed with [[BC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Zenit inks Jordan Mickey |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Euroleague/news/692346/Zenit-inks-Jordan-Mickey |website=Eurobasket |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=July 4, 2021}}</ref>

He left the team after the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/591726/guerre-en-ukraine-ces-joueurs-etrangers-qui-nont-pas-quitte-les-equipes-russes-engagees-en-euroleague/|title=Guerre en Ukraine: ces joueurs étrangers qui n'ont pas quitté les équipes russes engagées en Euroleague | Basket Europe|date=March 11, 2022}}</ref>

=== Virtus Bologna (2022–2024) ===
On July 13, 2022, Mickey signed with [[Virtus Bologna]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-13 |title=JORDAN MICKEY IS A NEW VIRTUS SEGAFREDO BOLOGNA PLAYER! |url=https://www.virtus.it/en/news/jordan-mickey-is-a-new-virtus-segafredo-bologna-player/ |access-date=2022-07-14 |language=en-US}}</ref> On 29 September 2022, after having ousted [[Olimpia Milano]] in the semifinals, Virtus won its [[2022 Italian Basketball Supercup|third Supercup]], defeating 72–69 [[Dinamo Sassari|Banco di Sardegna Sassari]] and achieving a back-to-back, following the 2021 trophy.<ref>{{cite web |title=Supercoppa, trionfa la Virtus Bologna! Canestro decisivo di Mickey, Sassari cede 72-69|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Basket/SerieA/29-09-2022/basket-supercoppa-trionfa-virtus-bologna-sassari-ko-72-69-450409276762.shtml|website=Gazzetta dello Sport|date=29 September 2022}}</ref> However, despite good premises Virtus ended the [[2022–23 EuroLeague|EuroLeague season]] at the 14th place, thus it did not qualify for the playoffs.<ref>[https://bolognabasket.org/virtus-il-punto-a-fine-eurolega/ Virtus, il punto a fine EuroLega]. BolognaBasket</ref> Moreover, the team was defeated in the [[Italian Basketball Cup]] final by [[Pallacanestro Brescia|Brescia]]. In June, after having ousted 3–0 both Brindisi and Tortona, Virtus was defeated 4–3 by Olimpia Milan in the national finals, following a series which was widely regarded among the best in the latest years of Italian basketball.<ref>[https://video.repubblica.it/sport/basket-milano-batte-bologna-nella-decisiva-gara-7-e-vince-il-suo-30esimo-scudetto-gli-highlights/447915/448883 Basket, Milano batte Bologna nella decisiva gara 7 e vince il suo 30esimo scudetto. Gli highlights]. la Repubblica</ref><ref>[https://www.rainews.it/articoli/2023/06/basket-serie-a-playoff-olimpia-milano-batte-virtus-bologna-in-gara-7-e-vince-lo-scudetto-al-forum-assago-c279332e-c2fa-46be-a199-3ff966b78a99.html Basket, Milano batte Bologna 67-55 nella finalissima e si conferma campione per la trentesima volta]. Rai News</ref>

On 24 September 2023, after having ousted Olimpia Milano in the semifinals, Virtus won its [[2023 Italian Basketball Supercup|fourth Supercup]], and the third in a row, defeating 97–60 [[Pallacanestro Brescia|Germani Brescia]].<ref>[https://bologna.repubblica.it/sport/2023/09/24/news/una_virtus_esagerata_stravince_la_supercoppa-415671857/ Una Virtus esagerata stravince la Supercoppa]. la Repubblica</ref>

=== Qingdao Eagles (2024–present) ===
On November 6, 2024, Mickey signed with [[Qingdao Eagles]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA),<ref>{{cite web |title=青岛男篮官宣外援乔丹·米奇加盟 |url=https://www.qdxin.cn/sports/2024/347119.html |website=信网 |access-date=6 November 2024 |date=6 November 2024}}</ref> replaced [[Akil Mitchell]].<ref>{{cite web |title=青岛男篮更换内线外援，米切尔被裁前凯尔特人悍将已到队 |url=https://news.bandao.cn/a/1730813013083733.html |publisher=大众·半岛新闻 |access-date=15 November 2024 |date=5 November 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Mickey is the son of James Wright and Torand Hunter. His father played [[Center (basketball)|center]] for [[Abilene Christian Wildcats men's basketball|Abilene Christian University]] and was the [[Lone Star Conference]] MVP in 1984–85.<ref name="draft-profile" />
